From 1974 the government of Ferdinand Marcos began sending Filipino workers abroad on contracts, starting with construction crews for the oil-rich Gulf states. Labour export became a national policy.

Today about ten million Filipinos live or work abroad: nurses in the United States and Britain, domestic workers in Hong Kong and the Middle East, and seafarers, who crew a large share of the world's merchant ships.

The money they send home is about a tenth of the economy. It has built houses and paid school fees, but it also splits families. Filipinos call them modern heroes. See Philippines and older labour migrations.
